summary: Berezovo Airport (EZV) is a medium-sized regional airport serving the town of Berezovo in the Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Okrug of western Siberia, Russia. Situated in a remote, sub-Arctic region known for its oil and gas industry, the airport provides essential connectivity for residents and workers in this isolated part of the country. It primarily handles domestic flights and operates as a vital lifeline for the local community given the challenging overland travel conditions.
faqs:
Q: Where is Berezovo Airport located?
A: Berezovo Airport is located near the town of Berezovo in the Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Okrug in western Siberia, Russia.

Q: What is the airport primarily used for?
A: The airport primarily serves domestic passenger flights, connecting this remote Siberian community with larger Russian cities.

Q: When is the best time to fly to Berezovo?
A: Summer months (June to August) offer the most reliable flying conditions, as the region experiences extremely harsh winters with heavy snowfall and sub-zero temperatures that can cause delays.

Q: Are there car rental services at the airport?
A: Rental car options are limited at Berezovo Airport; most visitors arrange ground transportation through local hotels or pre-booked services.
transport_tips: The airport is located a short drive from the town center, typically accessible by taxi or pre-arranged transfer. Public transportation options are limited, so arranging a pickup in advance is highly recommended, especially during winter months when weather conditions can be severe. Many visitors traveling for the oil and gas industry have transport coordinated by their employers.
local_tip: Pack warm layers in your carry-on even during summer flights, as the airport terminal can feel chilly and weather in the region can change rapidly.
